sections.overview: The Great Oak Beauty is a geometrid moth of oak woodland, recorded in southern England and Wales.
sections.identification: UKMoths gives a 40–50 mm wingspan; its cryptic brown pattern blends with bark and twigs.
sections.habitat: It inhabits oak woodland. In southern England, it is especially associated with ancient and mature woods.
sections.diet: The caterpillar feeds on oak. A Hampshire account specifies pedunculate oak.
sections.behavior: Adults fly mainly in June and July and come to light; resting caterpillars resemble twigs.
sections.reproduction: The larva overwinters; the sources give no complete mating or egg-laying schedule.
sections.ecology: It is associated with oak as a larval food plant; the related Pale Oak Beauty, Hypomecis punctinalis, can be confused with it but has a ring-shaped hindwing mark.
sections.conservation: Hampshire and Isle of Wight records report local declines linked to habitat destruction, but this regional account is not a global assessment.
